question: What cycle and cooling arrangement describes the Thielert TAE 125 engine?

options.text: A liquid-cooled, four-stroke Diesel-cycle engine with wet sump lubrication
An air-cooled, four-stroke Otto-cycle engine with dry sump lubrication
A liquid-cooled, two-stroke Diesel-cycle engine with wet sump lubrication
An air-cooled, four-stroke Diesel-cycle engine with wet sump lubrication

explanation: The TAE 125 is a liquid-cooled four-stroke Diesel-cycle engine with wet sump lubrication, in-line construction and common-rail direct injection.

question: What is the propeller speed-reducing gear ratio of the TAE 125 engine?
explanation: The engine drives the propeller through a speed-reducing gearbox at a ratio of 1:1.69.

question: What is the displacement of the TAE 125-01 engine?
explanation: The TAE 125-01 displaces 1689 cm3; the later TAE 125-02-99 is a larger 1991 cm3 engine.

question: What is the displacement of the TAE 125-02-99 engine?
explanation: The TAE 125-02-99 displaces 1991 cm3, larger than the original TAE 125-01's 1689 cm3.

question: Even with the battery disconnected from the electrical distribution system by the ELECTRIC MASTER switch, what continues to receive electrical power directly from the battery?

options.text: The ECU
The avionics bus
The landing light
The pitot heat

explanation: The ECU receives its electrical power from the battery even if the ELECTRIC MASTER switch has disconnected the battery from the rest of the power distribution system.

question: What does the power lever directly command in the DA 40 D's engine control system?

options.text: The fuel/air mixture ratio directly
The desired engine power LOAD, expressed as a percentage
The propeller RPM directly, bypassing the ECU
The manifold pressure directly, bypassing the ECU

explanation: The power lever sets the desired engine power LOAD (%); the ECU then controls manifold pressure, injected fuel quantity and propeller speed to deliver it.

question: Following a loss of oil pressure in the propeller governor's separate oil circuit, what happens to the propeller blades?

options.text: They feather completely, stopping the propeller
They remain fixed at their last commanded pitch
They go to the finest possible pitch, giving maximum RPM
They go to the coarsest possible pitch, giving minimum RPM

explanation: A loss of governor oil pressure drives the blades to the finest possible pitch (maximum RPM), which is why the defective RPM regulating system procedure exists.

question: What are the three positions of the ELECTRIC MASTER key switch?

options.text: OFF, ON, ESSENTIAL
OFF, ARM, ON
ON, ECU A, ECU B
OFF, ON, START

explanation: ELECTRIC MASTER has three positions: OFF (disconnecting battery power), ON (connecting battery power to the distribution system), and START (starting the engine).

question: For normal operation, in which position is the ECU SWAP switch set, and which ECU then controls the engine?

options.text: AUTOMATIC, controlled by ECU A
AUTOMATIC, controlled by ECU B
ECU A, manually selected
ECU B, manually selected

explanation: Normal operation is with ECU SWAP set to AUTOMATIC, under which the engine is controlled by ECU A, switching automatically to ECU B on a failure.

question: With the power lever at IDLE and RPM below approximately 900, what does pressing and holding the ECU TEST button start?

options.text: A test of the pitot heat system
The self-test of the engine control unit
A test of the propeller governor only
A reset of the low fuel caution

explanation: At IDLE with RPM below about 900, ECU TEST starts the ECU self-test, cycling from ECU A to ECU B and back while the propeller cycles.

question: During the ECU Backup Battery test (IFR-equipped airplanes), if the battery's capacity is found to be less than 70 percent of rated capacity, what happens?

options.text: The ENGINE caution light illuminates instead
The test simply cannot be completed and no light is shown
The 'ECU BACKUP UNSAFE' light is on continuously
The 'ECU BACKUP UNSAFE' light blinks three times then extinguishes

explanation: If the ECU Backup Battery tests below 70 percent of rated capacity, the 'ECU BACKUP UNSAFE' light stays on continuously rather than extinguishing at the end of the test.

question: What is the purpose of the ALTERNATE AIR lever, and what is its normal position?

options.text: It routes cabin air to the turbocharger for extra cooling, and is normally open (rearward)
It opens a second fuel injector bank, and is normally closed (forward)
It controls cowl flaps for engine cooling, and is normally open (rearward)
It draws air from the engine compartment if the normal intake is blocked, and is normally closed (forward)

explanation: ALTERNATE AIR draws air from the engine compartment in case of icing or a blocked air filter; the lever is normally forward (closed) and is pulled to the rear to open it.

question: What indications does the Compact Engine Display (CED 125) provide?

options.text: RPM, oil pressure, oil temperature, coolant temperature, gearbox temperature and LOAD
Fuel quantity in both tanks, fuel temperature and fuel flow
Ammeter, voltmeter and WATER LEVEL only
Airspeed, altitude and vertical speed for the engine

explanation: The CED 125 shows RPM, oil pressure (OP), oil temperature (OT), coolant temperature (CT), gearbox temperature (GT) and LOAD.

question: Which indications appear on the Auxiliary Engine Display (AED 125) rather than the CED 125?

options.text: LOAD and propeller RPM
Fuel quantity, fuel temperature, generator current, volts and fuel flow
RPM, oil pressure and oil temperature
Coolant temperature and gearbox temperature

explanation: The AED 125 carries fuel-related and electrical indications - fuel quantity (MAIN/AUX), WATER LEVEL, fuel temperature left/right, GENERATOR current, VOLT and FUEL FLOW - while the CED 125 carries the core engine parameters.

question: At approximately what coolant temperature does the thermostat valve activate the radiator, ending the warm-up bypass?

options.text: Approximately 96 degrees C
Approximately 105 degrees C
Approximately 80 degrees C
Approximately 60 degrees C

explanation: The bypass cooler allows warm-up until the thermostat activates the radiator at approximately 80 degrees C.

question: Is the flow through the coolant-to-air heat exchanger for cabin heating dependent on coolant temperature?

options.text: Yes, it only flows once the thermostat opens the radiator
Yes, it is proportional to coolant temperature
No, cabin heat uses a separate electric heater unrelated to coolant
No, the flow through the heat exchanger is independent of coolant temperature

explanation: The coolant-to-air heat exchanger for cabin heat receives flow independent of coolant temperature, unlike the radiator bypass.

question: What protects the cooling system against overpressure?

options.text: A pressure relief valve, with an expansion tank to adjust system pressure
A thermostat valve alone
The radiator bypass valve
The waste gate valve

explanation: An expansion tank helps adjust pressure and a pressure relief valve protects the cooling system against overpressure.

question: What controls the waste gate valve that bypasses excess exhaust gas around the turbine?

options.text: The propeller governor
The ECU, using a manifold pressure sensor behind the compressor
A mechanical spring-loaded valve with no electronic control
The pilot, via the ALTERNATE AIR lever

explanation: The ECU controls the waste gate valve using a manifold pressure sensor behind the compressor, preventing excessive manifold pressure at low density altitudes.

question: After being compressed by the turbocharger, why is the intake air cooled in the intercooler before entering the engine?

options.text: It reduces the fuel temperature in the common rail
It prevents icing of the manifold pressure sensor
Cooling the air increases its density, increasing engine efficiency and power
It prevents the glow plugs from overheating

explanation: Cooling the compressed intake air in the intercooler increases its density, which increases power through greater efficiency.

question: How many separate oil systems does the engine have?

options.text: One combined system serving the engine, turbocharger and propeller governor
Three: engine lubrication, turbocharger lubrication, and gearbox lubrication
Two: engine lubrication and turbocharger lubrication, with the governor supplied by hydraulic fluid
Two: engine/turbocharger lubrication, and the gearbox/propeller governor system

explanation: The engine has two separate oil systems: the wet-sump engine/turbocharger lubrication system, and a second circuit for the gearbox and propeller governor.

question: Where is the inspection glass used to check gear oil quantity located?

options.text: Behind an inspection hole on the front side of the lower cowling
Behind an inspection hole in the upper cowling, next to the engine oil dipstick
Inside the cabin, next to the power lever
On the propeller spinner

explanation: Gear oil quantity is checked through an inspection glass reached via an inspection hole on the front of the lower cowling, separate from the engine oil dipstick in the upper cowling.

question: Which of the following is one of the sensor inputs the ECU uses to control and regulate the engine?

options.text: Landing gear position
Power lever position, sensed twice for redundancy
Outside air temperature at the pitot probe
Flap position

explanation: Among its many sensor inputs, the ECU reads power lever position twice (for redundancy), along with oil/coolant/gearbox temperature, oil pressure, camshaft and crankshaft RPM (each twice), fuel and manifold pressure, and more.

question: Which of the following is one of the outputs the ECU sends to control the engine?

options.text: A signal to the landing gear actuator
A signal to the autopilot servo
A signal for the waste gate valve
A signal to the flap motor

explanation: ECU outputs include activation of the starter relay, the propeller governor pressure valve, the rail-pressure regulation valve, each of the 4 injection nozzles, the glow plugs, and the waste gate valve.

question: Under normal conditions, which ECU controls and regulates the engine, with the other acting as backup?

options.text: ECU B controls the engine normally; ECU A is the backup for redundancy
Both ECUs share control simultaneously at all times
Neither controls alone; a majority-vote system between both is used
ECU A controls the engine normally; ECU B is the backup for redundancy

explanation: ECU A normally controls and regulates the engine; ECU B exists purely as a backup to ensure redundancy.

question: If the loss of a sensor signal caused an automatic switch from ECU A to ECU B, what happens once that signal returns?

options.text: The system automatically switches back to ECU A
The system remains on ECU B until the next flight
The pilot must manually select ECU A using the ECU SWAP switch
The system alternates between ECU A and ECU B every few minutes

explanation: If a lost sensor signal was the cause of the switch-over, the system automatically switches back to ECU A once that signal is restored.

question: After an ECU A/B FAIL caution message has been displayed, what is required even if the caution could be reset?

options.text: The airplane may fly one more flight before servicing
The engine must be serviced
No further action is needed once reset
Only a logbook entry is required, with servicing optional

explanation: Once an ECU A/B FAIL caution has appeared, the engine must be serviced afterward, whether or not the caution message could be reset in flight.
